citeAs: Conneau, A., Ma, M., Khanuja, S., Zhang, Y., Axelrod, V., Dalmia, S., Riesa, J., Rivera, C., Bapna, A. (2022). FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech. arXiv.
creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna (Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University)
description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the FLoRes-101 machine translation benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It provides human speech recordings and transcripts for tasks including automatic speech recognition, speech language identification, translation, and retrieval.
name: FLEURS
rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings were collected for each sentence in each language, by three different native speakers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Recordings were collected from three different native speakers per sentence, with a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper describes quality control in which each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it matched the input sentence, and invalid recordings were discarded.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence in the 102 languages, the authors collected three recordings by three different native speakers. After recording, each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponded to the input sentence, and invalid recordings were discarded.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed with a balance in terms of sex ratio of at least 30/70% when possible. The paper also notes uneven performance across language groups related in part to differing amounts of available pre-training data, and tokenization mismatch for some scripts.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by starting from the FLoRes-101 dataset, using the public dev and devtest sets totaling 2009 translated sentences across 102 languages. For each sentence, three native speakers were asked to record spoken utterances, and recordings were subsequently validated by additional workers.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source text comes from FLoRes-101: 2009 sentences from the dev and devtest sets, originally extracted from English Wikipedia and translated by human translators into 101 languages. The speech data consists of raw recordings of speakers reading these sentences at 16 kHz.
rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The paper also reports worse performance for some unseen languages and for certain writing systems such as CJK and Urdu-related script issues, indicating limitations in coverage and representational difficulty.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors split the 2009 sentences into new train, dev, and test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively, and then split collected recordings into train, dev, and test with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test and a target ratio of 7:1:2. They state that recordings were kept as-is without data augmentations.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors provide tokenized sentence versions and preprocess text by applying NFC and FST normalization, lowercasing, normalizing and removing punctuation, splitting words into characters, and defining word boundaries. For each sentence they provide raw transcript (SRC RAW), preprocessed transcript (SRC NORM), and character-based transcript (SRC CHAR).
rai:dataUseCases: FLEURS is intended for evaluating multilingual speech technology tasks including automatic speech recognition, speech language identification, speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation, and multilingual speech-to-text and text-to-speech retrieval.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes speaker sex ratio information used during collection, and the paper discusses speaker-disjoint train/dev/test splits.
